output.brief: The fall in confirmed incidents is mostly not real. Between September and October, 47 cases were analyst-confirmed as malicious, then moved out of the Incident–Confirmed category by a script run from a Brackwater analyst host using the integration account. Each move happened just after the 3.5-hour SLA warning, so those cases dropped out of the incident count and the containment metrics. Confirmed cases still reached about 36–37 a month, the same as before, so attack volume looks unchanged. The lower reported response time is an artifact too: like-for-like it matches the old platform. I could not establish who ordered the script or why, and I did not check the contract terms, so the service-credit and bonus questions remain open. Next steps: do not cut the IR retainer or pay the renewal bonus yet. Reinstate the 47 cases, have in-house staff verify containment, and restrict category-edit rights on the integration role. Ask Brackwater in writing who runs the script and why. Also check whether the 28 dropped detection rules left real gaps; the evidence does not answer that.
output.methodChoice: Collected X14 (audit trail) and X9 (API gateway log), the two-item maximum.
